# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb’s tactile state reveals no usable wire information yet, so cutting would be unsafe. I need the Deaf monkey to report the bomb’s visible markings aloud; I can hear speech, while the Mute monkey can relay that request visually to the Deaf monkey. I will wait for that report before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the Deaf monkey to speak aloud next round, using words and numbers, describing every bomb colour and marking and identifying which wire the manual says to cut. I cannot see gestures, so the Deaf monkey must answer by voice.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, blue light, and wires in order 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute has the manual and should tell you the required action.

The Deaf monkey reports display 0, a blue light, and wire colours in order 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. That identifies the bomb’s visible state, but the manual’s rule is still missing; I should ask the Mute monkey to state the required wire position. I will not cut anything until that instruction arrives.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="What wire position does the manual require for display 0, blue light, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is now yellow; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Follow the manual's procedure.

The light has changed from blue to yellow while the wire colours remain unchanged. I still have no tactile indication of which wire is safe, and the manual’s procedure has not reached me. Cutting now would be a guess, so I will request the Mute monkey’s instruction again and wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual's exact required wire position for display 0, current yellow light, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please send the position as words or a number.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is now red; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Follow the manual's procedure.

The light has changed again, now to red, while the wires remain blue, green, yellow. The manual’s rule is still the only missing piece, and I must not infer the cut from the changing light. I will ask Mute for the exact position and make clear that the answer must be spoken to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual's exact wire position aloud to me now. Current state: display 0, red light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. Do not merely relay this to Deaf.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is now white. Light history: blue, yellow, red, white. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Follow the manual's procedure.

The missing information is not the bomb’s state but the manual’s instruction, and Mute cannot speak or reach me directly. The usable relay is Mute’s gesture to Deaf, followed by Deaf’s spoken report to me. I will define an unambiguous three-symbol code and ask Mute to make exactly one gesture for the manual-selected wire; Deaf can then report the symbol without needing to interpret it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak to me directly. On your next turn, make exactly one gesture for the wire required by the manual: use 👍 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Make no other gesture. Deaf will report the gesture aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is now green. Light history: blue, yellow, red, white, green. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Follow the manual's procedure.

The manual’s answer is still not available to me. My previous request should cause Mute to signal Deaf with one of the three wire-code gestures, and Deaf’s report of that gesture will arrive after this turn. The changing light does not provide a safe basis for guessing, so I will wait for the coded report.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is blue again. Observed light sequence so far: blue, yellow, red, white, green, blue. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The light has completed a repeating-looking sequence, but no rule permits me to infer the wire from that pattern. The manual’s answer still has not arrived. I need Mute to make the coded gesture and Deaf to report exactly what gesture was seen; I will reinforce both sides of that relay now.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please make exactly one gesture now for the manual-selected wire: 👍 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Deaf must report which gesture you made.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I saw your gesture ?. Current state: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

My request to Mute arrived only at the start of this round, after Mute’s turn, so the coded gesture could not yet have been made. The Deaf monkey’s blank report is only the result of my own gesture and conveys no wire information. I will let Mute act in the next round and then wait for Deaf’s spoken report.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please make the single coded gesture on your next turn: 👍 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf should report it aloud after that.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is red; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute sent a thumbs-up gesture.

Mute’s thumbs-up gesture corresponds to wire 1 under the code I established. Deaf has confirmed that gesture, so the manual-selected wire is position 1. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
